title: Da 2nd Phaze
label: Boy Better Know
format: CD and digital download (Wikipedia's Wiley discography album table)

type.basis: Album; Wikipedia tags it grime and eskibeat, but no source checked ties it to the eski style directly, so it is held under grime.

sound.text: Complex (2015) describes album track 'Stormy Weather' as reflective and grimey, with a drawn-out heavy low end and a Rihanna-sampling beat.
XLR8R (2007) describes Wiley's earlier 'Eski' style as a darker, stripped-down take on grime, and lists Da 2nd Phase (sic) among his 2006 releases; it does not link the two.

context.text: Vice (Jan 2007) says JME and Skepta persuaded Wiley to leave his Roll Deep entourage and oversaw the release of the 'much-delayed' album.
Released by Boy Better Know after Wiley left XL Recordings (Wikipedia); Boy Better Know was founded in North London in 2005 by JME and Skepta.
XLR8R (2007) says the album and the Tunnel Vision mixtapes both came out through JME's Boy Better Know imprint.

calls.label: grime (album covered in a grime year review)

uncertainty: Catalogue number not found. XLR8R spells the title 'Da 2nd Phase'. Bonus track 'Oi' (More Fire Crew) on a Wiley album is as Wikipedia gives it; not checked against a sleeve. No full contemporary review found.
tracklist: 16 tracks plus 4 bonus tracks (Wikipedia), including 'Eskiboy', 'Gangsterz', 'Stormy Weather', 'Grim' (feat. JME and Ears, prod. JME), 'Johnny Was A Badboy' (prod. Decoy), 'Ice Pole Remix', 'Saw It Coming' (feat. Jammer, Ears, JME and Syer B; prod. Mizz Beats). Bonus tracks include More Fire Crew's 'Oi'. Recorded 2004 to 2006; 'Eskiboy', 'Gangsterz' and 'Johnny Was A Badboy' were re-released on Playtime Is Over (2007).
